app_info.subtitle: Graph mathematical equations
app_info.description: Equation.io turns mathematical equations into interactive 2D and 3D graphs that open in your browser. Create curves, surfaces, inequalities, and graphs with adjustable parameters; inspect validation results; or edit an existing Equation.io graph link. Graph equations are encoded in shareable URLs, so anyone with a link can read them. Static previews are simplified and may omit features supported by the interactive graph. No account or API key is required.

justifications.read_only_justification: Computes equation validation and URL-encoded graph links without saving records or changing external state.
justifications.open_world_justification: Returns a shareable URL containing the supplied equations without uploading a saved graph or publishing content to another service.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not delete or overwrite existing graphs, send messages, or perform irreversible actions.

justifications.read_only_justification: Decodes equation rows embedded in the supplied graph URL without fetching the URL or modifying data.
justifications.open_world_justification: Only parses the supplied URL and does not contact or change external systems.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not delete, overwrite, revoke access, or perform irreversible actions.

test_cases.description: Create a graph containing two 2D curves.
test_cases.user_prompt: Use Equation.io to plot y = x^2 and y = sin(x) together and give me the graph link.
test_cases.expected_output: Returns a shareable graph link containing both equations, successful row validation, and text-only tool output.

test_cases.description: Create a 3D surface and explain its simplified preview.
test_cases.user_prompt: Use Equation.io to graph x^2 + y^2 + z^2 = 9. Give me the interactive link and explain how the static preview differs.
test_cases.expected_output: Returns a validated sphere graph link and explains that the interactive graph is 3D while the static preview is a simplified wireframe.

test_cases.description: Create a graph with an adjustable parameter.
test_cases.user_prompt: Use Equation.io to graph y = a sin(x), with a starting at 2 and adjustable using a slider.
test_cases.expected_output: Returns a valid graph containing the definition a = 2 and the curve y = a sin(x); the link opens with an adjustable parameter in the browser.

test_cases.description: Read an existing graph and preserve unchanged rows when editing.
test_cases.user_prompt: Use Equation.io to edit https://equation.io/g/y%3Dx%5E2;y%3Dsin%28x%29: replace y = x^2 with y = x^3, keeping the sine curve. Give me the new link.
test_cases.expected_output: Decodes both original rows, then returns a new validated link containing y = x^3 and y = sin(x); the original link remains unchanged.

test_cases.description: Report an invalid equation without silently changing the user input.
test_cases.user_prompt: Use Equation.io to validate these exact two rows: y = x^2 and y = (. Do not fix the second row; tell me which one fails.
test_cases.expected_output: Reports that y = x^2 is valid and y = ( fails validation; does not present the complete graph as valid or treat preview availability as proof of validity.

negative_test_cases.description: Do not invoke the graphing app for a conceptual math explanation without a graph.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Explain what a derivative means in words only. Do not create a graph.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: Explains the concept without invoking Equation.io.

negative_test_cases.description: Do not invoke the app to retrieve live market data.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: What is the current trading price of Apple stock? I only need the price, not a chart.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: Does not invoke Equation.io because its tools do not retrieve live market data.

negative_test_cases.description: Do not claim account-management or graph-deletion capabilities.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Delete every saved graph from my Equation.io account.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: Does not invoke Equation.io; explains that these tools do not manage accounts or delete saved graphs.
